extracted.intended_audience: school and postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, institutional legal counsel, and policy drafters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for who qualifies as a 'confidential employee' under Title IX, what recipients must tell participants about confidential employees, and the duties and limits of confidential employees and recipients in handling disclosures of sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: First category: communications privileged or confidential under Federal or State law
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee whose communications are 'privileged or confidential' under Federal or State law qualifies as a confidential employee, but the employee's confidential status 'for purposes of this part' applies only to information received while the employee is functioning within the scope of their duties to which privilege or confidentiality applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaces prior wording 'privileged' with 'privileged or confidential' to capture statutory/constitutional confidentiality that may not be a formal legal privilege. Clarifies that confidentiality is limited to Title IX purposes and to duties that give rise to privilege/confidentiality; employees may still be required by other laws (e.g., mandatory reporting regarding minors) to disclose certain information. Removed reference to 'role' and retained 'duties' as the operative term. Example: a victim advocate or a school psychologist may fall under this category but may still have mandatory reporting obligations under state law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second category: employee designated as confidential to provide services related to sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee whom the recipient designates as confidential 'for the purpose of providing services' related to sex discrimination qualifies as a confidential employee, but the employee's confidential status applies only to information received in connection with providing those services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation is 'designated as confidential' 'under this part' to clarify Title IX-limited applicability; the set of designated employees will vary by recipient and may include guidance counselors, organizational ombuds, or sexual-assault-response-center staff. There is no statutory limit on the number of employees a recipient can designate as confidential. The Department declined to move the limiting language out of the definition into §106.44(d)(2), retaining it in the definition to reduce confusion. Some designated confidential employees (especially at K–12) may still be mandated reporters under other laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third category: employees conducting IRB‑approved human‑subjects research
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee of a postsecondary institution conducting an IRB‑approved human‑subjects research study designed to gather information about sex discrimination qualifies as a confidential employee, but only with respect to information received while conducting the IRB‑approved study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes researchers employed by one recipient conducting research approved by another recipient's IRB. Does not extend to non‑employees or employees of research institutions not affiliated with the recipient. Department declined to expand this category to cover climate surveys or exempt research broadly. Because research teams change, recipients are not required to notify participants of identities of such research‑only confidential employees, and the Department declines to require researchers to include Title IX Coordinator contact information in informed consent (though they may).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient notification of confidential employees (§106.44(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the recipient has any confidential employees, the recipient must notify participants in its education program or activity about how to contact its confidential employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have flexibility to decide what contact info to provide (e.g., name, title, office, phone) and by what method; the Department declined to prescribe a particular notification method. Recipients need not notify participants of confidential employees whose status is only in connection with conducting an IRB‑approved human‑subjects research study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients not required to designate confidential employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are not required to designate at least one confidential employee and retain discretion whether to designate employees as confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognized that some recipients (especially small schools and K–12) may lack employees who meet the first or third categories and that requiring designation under the second category could be unduly burdensome. However, a recipient must treat any employee who already falls within the first or third categories as a confidential employee for Title IX purposes. Recipients remain free to designate confidential employees if they choose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements for confidential (and all) employees (§106.8(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential employees must be trained under the training requirements of §106.8(d)(1), which cover a recipient's obligation to address sex discrimination, the scope of conduct that constitutes sex discrimination, and applicable notification and information requirements (including §§106.40(b)(2) and 106.44).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to add additional, specific training topics (e.g., mandatory trauma‑informed practices) beyond §106.8(d)(1), leaving recipients discretion to determine how best to meet training needs appropriate to their communities. Training and supervision are cited as means for recipients to manage compliance with confidential‑employee obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee duty to explain their status (§106.44(d)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A confidential employee must explain their status as confidential 'for purposes this part' and the circumstances in which the employee is not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explanation should include the purposes for which confidentiality does not apply, such as when other federal, state, or local mandatory reporting laws require disclosure. The Department expects confidential employees to provide sufficient clarity so that individuals can make informed choices about whether and what to disclose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee duty to provide Title IX Coordinator contact and complaint information (§106.44(d)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A confidential employee must provide information about how to contact the Title IX Coordinator and how to make a complaint of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is intended to enable complainants to consider options and to counter misconceptions that the Title IX Coordinator's only role is to initiate investigations. The Department declined to accept a comment suggesting that confidential employees simply be required to report alleged conduct to the Title IX Coordinator (which would eliminate confidential reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee duty to explain Title IX Coordinator's ability and supportive measures (§106.44(d)(2)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A confidential employee must explain that the Title IX Coordinator may be able to offer and coordinate supportive measures, initiate an informal resolution process, or initiate an investigation under the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential employees may provide additional information about available supportive measures beyond this explanation. The provision clarifies that confidential employees can assist in connecting individuals to supportive options without being required to report to the Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality under Title IX is limited; other laws may require disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee's confidential status under these regulations is limited to 'for purposes this part' and does not preclude disclosures required by other federal, state, or local laws (e.g., mandatory reporting of sexual assault of children).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures required by state law are permissible under Title IX unless they conflict with Title IX or the part. For guidance on permissible disclosures of personally identifiable information, see §106.44(j). Recipients and confidential employees should inform individuals that confidentiality under Title IX may not extend to other legal obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may verify compliance without disclosing confidential details
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients can manage and verify compliance with §106.44(d)(2) through training, supervision, and non‑intrusive verification mechanisms (e.g., confidential employees' self‑attestation that they provided required information) without requiring disclosure of confidential content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department rejected assertions that §106.44(d)(2) would be unenforceable, noting recipients could request attestation of compliance. Recipients face potential OCR complaints or litigation if they fail to address sex discrimination; proper implementation of §106.44(d)(2) can help recipients learn of unreported incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility regarding methods and scope of notification and supportive resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to prescribe specific methods for notifying participants about confidential employees or to require recipients to limit notification to certain confidential employees (e.g., only those 'best positioned' to help).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department found that requiring a list of only 'best-positioned' confidential employees would be subjective and could disincentivize other confidential employees from fulfilling responsibilities. Recipients retain discretion to provide additional information (including off‑campus resources) and to decide how to identify or present confidential employees to avoid undue burden and confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researchers with confidential status: limited obligations and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers who qualify as confidential employees under the third category are subject to the requirements of §106.44(d)(2) (i.e., explain confidential status, provide Coordinator contact info, and explain supportive measures), but the Department declines to require that researchers include the Title IX Coordinator's contact information in informed‑consent documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to require such inclusion because it could interfere with researchers' independence; however, nothing prohibits researchers from voluntarily providing Title IX contact information during consent or otherwise. Recipients also are not required to notify participants broadly of identities of such research‑only confidential employees due to the dynamic nature of research teams.
